title: Numbers from simple operations are intrinsically complex in any representation

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Numbers from simple operations are intrinsically complex in any representation

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: For any representation of numbers in which recovering the value takes comparable effort for all numbers, some numbers look simple but others produced by simple mathematical operations look random, so such numbers are often intrinsically complex independent of representation.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: numbers generated by simple mathematical operations are often in some intrinsic sense complex, independent of the particular representation that one uses to look at them.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 4, “Systems Based on Numbers”; section “Mathematical Constants” (from p. 136), p. 144. Scope: numbers generated by simple mathematical operations, across number representations

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch04-17: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.31

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Restricted algorithmic-information statements are mathematically meaningful, but the stated qualifier on representations is insufficient to yield a unique decision criterion. Computations on chosen encodings would not discriminate the universal philosophical conclusion from rivals.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: One could choose a formal class of value-decodable representations and compare description lengths of selected constants across them. No finite survey can establish representation-independent intrinsic complexity over the unrestricted representation class in the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Comparable effort and looks random are undefined.

Representation classes can be constructed to make any chosen number simple.

Intrinsic complexity depends on the computational model up to encoding constants.

fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.3
operationalizability: 0.22
data existence: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.18
discriminating power: 0.25

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Digits and continued fractions already show that the same constant can look simple in one representation and irregular in another, and both representations are computable or proved. The claim is about any representation in which recovering the value costs about the same for all numbers, which is a much larger class than the ones that have been checked. A short list of standard representations is a real partial test and leaves the universal wording open.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fix a small list of representations with comparable evaluation cost, such as integer-base digits and continued fractions, and test whether numbers defined by simple operations look simple in every representation or irregular in some. Irregularity in every representation on the list supports intrinsic complexity for those representations; a representation that simplifies all of them challenges the claim inside the list.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A representation can be designed to make any particular number look simple, and 'comparable effort' is hard to enforce across all representations.

'Often' and 'intrinsic' have no single decision threshold.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.6
operationalizability: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.45
discriminating power: 0.35
